methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Math CLIL Integration
content: The 80/40 Split: Every 120-minute session is divided into two distinct parts.
Math Component (40 mins): Taught first. Focuses strictly on learning the mathematical vocabulary and reading equations aloud through engaging contexts.
ELA Component (80 mins): Applies the math concepts into writing. Students learn the English skills needed to explain how they solved the math problem step-by-step.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (3 Sessions x 120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce the basic language of addition (plus, equals, sum) via a story about gathering magical items.
Session 2: Apply addition to real-life word problems (helping an animal). Teach students to identify "clue words" and explain their solving steps logically.
Session 3: Full synthesis. Students write a complete, cohesive explanatory report about working together to solve a practical problem.

parts.title: PART 1: MATH COMPONENT (40 Mins)
content: A. READING MATH INPUT [ALL]
The Magic Crystals
Detective Max is exploring a dark cave. He finds a heavy stone door. There are empty holes in the door.
Suddenly, Max finds 2 glowing blue crystals on the ground. Then, he looks behind a rock and finds 3 shiny red crystals!
To open the door, Max must put all the crystals together. He uses his "Plus Machine" gadget.
The gadget says: "You must ADD the crystals. 2 + 3 = ?"
Max reads the screen: "Two PLUS three EQUALS what?"
He puts them in the holes. Two plus three equals FIVE!
The door opens! The total SUM of the crystals is 5. Adding makes the number bigger!
B. MATH VOCABULARY BUILDING [ALL]
add (cộng): We _______________ (add / read) numbers to make them bigger.
plus (cộng): Three _______________ (plus / equals) four is seven.
equals (bằng): Four plus one _______________ (equals / adds) five.
sum (tổng): The _______________ (sum / plus) of two and two is four.
total (tổng cộng): Find the _______________ (total / equal) number.
C. MATH PRACTICE
[O] L1 — Match the math sentence to the English sentence (5 items)

[ Sub-total: _____ / 5 ]

parts.title: PART 2: ELA COMPONENT (80 Mins)

How to Explain the Magic

"Dear Luna, I found a math problem in the cave. Here is how I solved it.
First, I start with the number 2 for the blue crystals.
Next, I add 3 more for the red crystals.
Then, I count all the crystals together in my hand.
Finally, I write the answer in my notebook. The sum equals exactly 5!
Solving puzzles is easy when you explain it step by step!"

content: A. READING MATH INPUT [ALL]
Pip's Winter Acorns
Math detectives can help animals solve problems!
Look at this story: "Pip the squirrel is preparing for winter. He has 4 acorns in his tree. Today, he runs to the forest and finds 5 more acorns. How many acorns does Pip have in total?"
Pip is confused, so Detective Luna helps him.
First, she looks for the clue words. The words "more" and "in total" mean we must ADD.
The math equation is: 4 + 5 = ?
She reads: "Four plus five equals what?"
Let's find the total sum. Four plus five equals NINE. The sum is 9.
Pip is very happy. He has 9 acorns in total to eat this winter!
Word problems are just stories with hidden math!
B. MATH VOCABULARY BUILDING [ALL]

Then, I write the math equation on the board: 5 + 4 = 9.

content: A. READING MATH INPUT [ALL]
Building the Bridge
Welcome to my final presentation! I am Detective Luna.
Today, we will use addition to build a bridge across a small stream!
Max brings 5 strong wooden logs from the forest. I bring 5 more logs from the camp. We need to add them together to see if we have enough.
The equation is 5 + 5 = 10.
We read: "Five plus five equals ten."
The total sum equals 10 logs!
What if the stream is wider? We might need 10 logs and 2 more logs.
The equation is: 10 + 2 = 12.
We read: "Ten plus two equals twelve."
Addition helps us know how many things we have in total. The numbers can grow very big, and our bridge will be strong!
B. MATH VOCABULARY BUILDING [ALL]
Review of Tier 1 Words (Math):
add: You can add the wooden logs together.
plus: Ten plus two equals twelve.
equals: The sum equals ten logs!

First, I read the problem and find the clue word "total".
Next, I know that "total" means I must add.
Then, I write the numbers with a plus sign and an equals sign. Ten plus two equals twelve.
Finally, I count all the logs together and write the answer. The sum is twelve.
By explaining the steps clearly, we can solve any building problem in the forest.
Thank you for listening to my report!
E. ELA VOCABULARY BUILDING [ALL]
Review of Tier 1 Words (ELA):
